title: Social Media News Feed
summary: Design the home feed of a social network that shows posts from the people a user follows.
statement: Design a news feed for a social network. Users publish posts and follow others; each user sees a timeline of relevant posts. Include how posts reach followers, how the feed is ranked, and how celebrity accounts are handled. Start by clarifying requirements and estimating scale, then design the system and defend your decisions.
initialGuidance: Clarify the users, the main journeys, and what is explicitly out of scope before drawing anything.
Estimate read and write volume and storage growth; the numbers decide which components you need.
Name the guarantees you will offer (consistency, durability, availability) and the trade-offs behind them.
Write down assumptions as you make them and revisit them when requirements change.

requirementQuestions.question: How many users, posts per day, and feed views per day?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Sets read and write rates and storage growth, which decide whether a single node can cope.

requirementQuestions.question: What feed load time is expected and how fresh must new posts appear?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Defines which paths need caching, precomputation, or regional placement.

requirementQuestions.question: Is the feed chronological or ranked by relevance?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Fixes what is in and out of the design so effort goes to what matters.

requirementQuestions.question: What is the distribution of follower counts, including very popular accounts?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines the data model, retention, and storage choices.

requirementQuestions.question: Is it acceptable for a new post to appear for followers with a short delay?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Selects between strong and eventual models and shapes conflict handling.

requirementQuestions.question: Should the feed degrade (stale or partial) rather than fail?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines redundancy and failover design, and which features may degrade instead of failing.

workloadAssumptions.illustrativeNote: All numbers below are illustrative examples for practice and are not benchmarks. Real answers depend on the requirements the candidate negotiates.

items.name: Feed views per user per day

estimationPrompts: How many feed reads per second at peak?
How much storage do precomputed feeds need per user?
How many writes does one post by a celebrity cause under fan-out on write?

keyDecisions.question: When is the feed assembled?
considerations: Fan-out on write precomputes feeds and makes reads fast.
Fan-out on read computes at request time and avoids write amplification.

keyDecisions.question: Where are timelines stored?
considerations: Per-user lists of post IDs in a cache or key-value store.
Store IDs, hydrate content at read time.

keyDecisions.question: How is relevance computed?
considerations: Ranking uses features and a model, adding latency.

keyDecisions.question: How are follow relationships stored?
considerations: Both follower and followee lookups are needed.

keyDecisions.question: How are media and counters handled?
considerations: Media in object storage behind a CDN.
Like counters are write-hot; aggregate asynchronously.

tradeoffs.tension: Precomputing speeds reads but costs writes for popular authors.

commonMistakes: Fan-out on write for celebrities with millions of followers.
Computing every feed from scratch at read time with no caching.
Storing full post bodies in every timeline.
Ignoring deleted posts and blocked users in cached feeds.
followUps: How do you handle a user who follows thousands of accounts?
How would you add ads into the feed?
How do you keep the feed useful if the ranking service is down?
